_comment: Kibana alerting rules for the BIND dnstap data stream, loaded by load_alert_rules.py (setup.sh runs it when KIBANA_URL is set). All are Elasticsearch query rules (.es-query, available on every license) against the 'bind-dnstap-data-view' data view from bind-dashboards.ndjson, so the data view's runtime fields (dns.response_time_ms, dns.question.first_label_length) work in queries. Thresholds suit a small-to-medium site: tune 'threshold' and 'timeWindowSize' to your query volume, then re-run the loader (it updates rules in place by id).

rules.name: BIND: NXDOMAIN spike from a client
rules.why: One client getting a burst of 'no such domain' answers: malware cycling through generated domains (DGA), a scanner, or a badly misconfigured app.

rules.name: BIND: many distinct NXDOMAIN names under one domain

params._comment: ES|QL, because the query rule's KQL mode can't count distinct values. Fires (one alert listing the domains) whenever the query returns any row; edit the 50 to tune.
params.esql: FROM logs-bind.dnstap-* | WHERE event.action IN ("client_response", "auth_response") AND dns.response_code == "NXDOMAIN" AND dns.question.registered_domain IS NOT NULL | STATS distinct_names = COUNT_DISTINCT(dns.question.name), clients = COUNT_DISTINCT(client.ip) BY dns.question.registered_domain | WHERE distinct_names > 50 | SORT distinct_names DESC | LIMIT 10

rules.why: Lots of different non-existent names under one domain is the signature of DGA malware or a random-subdomain ('water torture') attack against that domain's servers. A broken app repeating one bad name doesn't trigger it.

rules.name: BIND: SERVFAIL / REFUSED spike
rules.why: A server failing to answer: upstream or forwarder problems, DNSSEC validation failures, or an ACL change refusing legitimate clients.

rules.name: BIND: slow answers
rules.why: Average time to answer clients above 500 ms on a server: slow or unreachable upstreams, a cold or undersized cache, or an overloaded server.

rules.name: BIND: possible DNS tunnelling (very long query labels)
rules.why: Repeated queries whose first label is 40+ characters: data being smuggled out encoded in DNS names, or some CDN/anti-spam lookups — check the names before acting.

rules.name: BIND: dnstap export stopped
rules.why: No answers indexed for 15 minutes: the converter timer (bind-dnstap-ndjson), Elastic Agent, or the pipeline has stopped — or all the BIND servers have.
